summary: Replaced the full HCP Editor ModuleJsonExportGenerator implementation with a thin subclass of Application\Composer\ModulesOverview\ModuleJsonExportGenerator.

The new subclass overrides only resolveModuleSource(): mistralys/* packages → 'framework', all others → 'hcp-editor'. All other workflow logic (module discovery, brief resolution, glossary building, glossary sections via DecorateGlossaryEvent, JSON output) is now fully inherited from the framework base class.
tools/generate-module-json.php continues to work: discovered and exported 42 modules successfully.
composer dump-autoload succeeded in both application-framework and hcp-editor.
PHPStan analysis passes with zero errors (3726 symbols analyzed).

comments.note: The old HCP Editor ModuleJsonExportGenerator duplicated ~180 lines that are now covered by the framework base class. The refactoring reduces the class to ~10 lines. No further observations — both the old and new code in the touched file are clean and consistent with project conventions.

summary: All 5 acceptance criteria verified and passing.
composer dump-autoload succeeds in both application-framework and hcp-editor.

tools/generate-module-json.php correctly discovers 42 module-context.yaml files: default mode outputs 14 modules (those with README-Brief.md), all classified as 'hcp-editor'; --all mode outputs all 42 with correct 'framework'/'hcp-editor' source classification confirming resolveModuleSource() logic is sound.
ModuleInfoTest (2 tests, 13 assertions), ModulesOverviewGenerator (13 tests, 146 assertions), and KeywordGlossaryGenerator (11 tests, 47 assertions) all pass without regressions.

The new glossarySections key in JSON output (1 section returned by DecorateGlossaryEvent) is correctly structured: heading, columnHeaders, entries. Addition is backward-compatible for existing consumers.

comments.note: No existing unit test covers ModuleJsonExportGenerator directly in hcp-editor. The tool is exercised end-to-end by generate-module-json.php. A dedicated test verifying resolveModuleSource() classification (framework vs hcp-editor) would strengthen the regression net. Not blocking.

The new glossarySections key in modules.json is not present in the old output but is backward-compatible (additional JSON keys do not break existing consumers). The DecorateGlossaryEvent listener contributes 1 section. Consumers of modules.json that don't consume this key are unaffected.

summary: Code review PASS. The HCP Editor ModuleJsonExportGenerator is a textbook thin subclass: ~35 lines including the docblock, clean override of resolveModuleSource() only, correct use of the extension point established in the framework base class. No blocking issues found across all four review dimensions (maintainability, best practices, performance, future context).

comments.note: The import alias `FrameworkModuleJsonExportGenerator` elegantly resolves the naming collision between the HCP Editor subclass and the framework base class without requiring a renamed class or a different namespace path. This is the correct idiomatic approach.

The `str_starts_with('mistralys/')` prefix check is simple, correct, and a single-responsibility implementation. The hardcoded vendor prefix string is the right design choice here — extracting it to a class constant would be mild over-engineering for what is a single fixed value with narrow purpose.

[documentation-forward] No dedicated unit test exists for resolveModuleSource() in hcp-editor. Both the Developer and QA flagged this. Coverage is end-to-end only via the CLI tool. A focused unit test (e.g., `testResolveModuleSourceClassifiesFrameworkPackage()` and `testResolveModuleSourceClassifiesHcpEditorPackage()`) would provide a regression safety net if the override logic is extended in future. Recommend adding to the Composer test suite in hcp-editor.
No observations — code is clean, well-documented, minimal, and consistent with project conventions. The thin subclass pattern used here is the ideal implementation of the framework extension point.
